prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Scholars agree that the niece who prepared the first published collection ______ the poems.

worlds.passage: When a poet died in 1902, she left 212 untitled poems loose in a desk drawer, with no instructions for what should become of them. Her niece sorted the loose sheets into three piles, love, faith, and the sea, and printed them in that sequence as a plain book of 212 pages, one poem to a page beneath its section heading. When the manuscripts were dated by their paper in 1990, scholars found an early poem about a shipwreck set beside a late one about drowning, each word just as the poet had left it. Scholars agree that the niece who prepared the first published collection ______ the poems.
worlds.explanation: Sorting the poems into piles by subject and printing them as sections means the niece "grouped" them. "Laundered" fails because each word was just as the poet left it; "illustrated" fails because it was a plain book; "interrupted" fails because each poem had its own page with nothing set into it.

laundered.quote: each word just as the poet had left it
laundered.why: the text was not cleaned up

illustrated.why: a plain book carries no pictures

interrupted.why: each poem stands whole on its page

worlds.passage: When a poet died in 1902, she left 212 untitled poems loose in a desk drawer, with no instructions for what should become of them. Her niece, a minister's wife, printed all 212 in the order she found them, as a plain book of one poem to a page. When the manuscripts resurfaced in 1990, scholars found that the poet's "God, if there is one" had become "God, who surely is," and that a dozen love poems addressed to a woman had been readdressed to "my brother." Scholars agree that the niece who prepared the first published collection ______ the poems.
worlds.explanation: Turning doubt into faith and readdressing love poems so they read respectably means the niece "laundered" them. "Grouped" fails because she kept the order she found them in; "illustrated" fails because it was a plain book; "interrupted" fails because each poem had its own page.

grouped.quote: in the order she found them

illustrated.why: a plain book carries no pictures

interrupted.why: the changes were hidden inside the lines, not breaks between them

worlds.passage: When a poet died in 1902, she left 212 untitled poems loose in a desk drawer, with no instructions for what should become of them. Her niece printed all 212 in the order she found them, and on the page facing each one a village engraver's woodcut shows the gull, the chapel, or the garden gate the poem names. Scholars who compared the book with the manuscripts in 1990 had no quarrel with its text; they regretted only that readers had come to picture her sea as the engraver's. Scholars agree that the niece who prepared the first published collection ______ the poems.
worlds.explanation: A woodcut facing each poem, showing what it names, means the niece "illustrated" the poems. "Grouped" fails because she kept the order she found them in; "laundered" fails because scholars had no quarrel with the text; "interrupted" fails because each picture sits on the facing page rather than breaking into the poem.

grouped.quote: in the order she found them

laundered.quote: had no quarrel with its text

interrupted.quote: on the page facing each one
interrupted.why: the images sit beside the poems, not within them

worlds.passage: When a poet died in 1902, she left 212 untitled poems loose in a desk drawer, with no instructions for what should become of them. Her niece printed all 212 in the order she found them, and after nearly every stanza she set down, in smaller type, a paragraph recalling where her aunt had been sitting that day or whom the lines concerned. A reviewer in 1903 complained that he could not get from one stanza to the next without learning what the weather had been. Scholars agree that the niece who prepared the first published collection ______ the poems.
worlds.explanation: Paragraphs after nearly every stanza kept readers from getting "from one stanza to the next," so the niece "interrupted" the poems. "Grouped" fails because she kept the order she found them in; "laundered" fails because her notes expose whom the lines concerned rather than disguising it; "illustrated" fails because what she added was type, not pictures.

grouped.quote: in the order she found them

laundered.why: she revealed the poems' private subjects rather than cleaning them up

illustrated.why: the additions were prose, not images
